Finding accidents using Geometric Invariant Theory The problem of finding accidents or custodial scalars can be phrased as follows: given a (or multiple) scalar(s) in some representation(s) of gauge group(s), can we find flat or almost flat directions on the vacuum manifold which are not spanned by the gauge group? In many cases this question can be answered using the toolbox provided by Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT). In this appendix we detail the geometric transcription of the problem and the main tools of GIT useful to our study in a rather informal way, for a more rigorous and in-depth review of GIT we refer to [40, 41].
